admin_whoami.title: Show the yaks.app account this box acts as
admin_whoami.description: The yaks.app account this box acts as, the kind it is (test, owner or admin), the person its session names, when that session expires, and every space it can reach with its role in each.

admin_accounts.title: List the yaks.app accounts signed in on this box
admin_accounts.description: Every yaks.app account this box holds a session for, with its kind and which test account is current. Never prints a session.

admin_throwaway.title: Sign in as a throwaway test account
admin_throwaway.description:
Sign this box in as a throwaway test account, <name>@bot.yak.sh, and make it current: every later admin command acts as it unless it names another account. Without a name, a fresh probe-<random> address. The sign-in code is read from the letter in this graph.

  yak admin throwaway
  yak admin throwaway cookbook

name.description: the local part of the address

admin_login.title: Sign in as a yaks.app account
admin_login.description:
Sign this box in as the yaks.app account at an address. A @bot.yak.sh code is read from the letter in this graph; anyone else’s is typed, or given with --code. Signing in as anybody but a test account is a named act: --owner for Jeff’s, --admin for admin@bot.yak.sh.

  yak admin login you@example.com --owner
  yak admin login admin@bot.yak.sh --admin

admin_use.title: Make a test account current
admin_use.description: Remember a test account as the one every later admin command acts as. An owner or admin account is refused: those are reached per command, with --owner or --admin.

account.description: the account, by address or local part

admin_logout.title: Forget a yaks.app account’s session
admin_logout.description: Forget the session this box holds for one yaks.app account. The bearer `yak login` keeps is `yak logout`.

account.description: the account, by address or local part

admin_link.title: Make a standing sign-in link
admin_link.description:
One URL that signs its holder in as this account until it expires, or --revoke to take one back by its id.

  yak admin throwaway reviewer && yak admin link --days=90
  yak admin link --revoke=3f2a --as=reviewer

revoke.description: a link id to revoke instead

admin_fee.title: Read or set the platform’s fee
admin_fee.description:
What the platform takes from a sale, in basis points: read it, or set it. The rate is the platform’s, so --admin or --owner is required.

  yak admin fee --admin
  yak admin fee 250 --owner

bps.description: the new rate, in whole basis points

admin_tunnel.title: Link a machine to a space
admin_tunnel.description:
The machine a space is linked to, whose door the space's apps reach through the link's gateway (a vpc_services door in their config). With no act, what the link is. connect makes a tunnel, its service to the door's port given, and the gateway; rotate gives the gateway a new secret, and the tunnel a new token where the platform made it; adopt records a tunnel and service made elsewhere with a gateway in front, and is the platform's act. Each keeps what it is answered in this graph's vault without printing it, the token as TUNNEL_TOKEN and the secret as LINK_SECRET, where @yaks/tunnel's service reads them. disconnect removes the link.

  yak admin tunnel yak --admin
  yak admin tunnel yak adopt --tunnel <id> --service <id> --admin
  yak admin tunnel ada connect --port 5174

act.description: what to change; nothing reads the link

port.description: connect: the port the machine's link door listens on

admin_delete.title: Close a space for good
admin_delete.description: Close a space: its apps, their data, and its address. What would go is listed first, the same list the confirmation letter carries to a person whose agent asked.

admin_query.title: Query an app’s store
admin_query.description:
An app’s store as this account reads it, through the filter grammar. `yak/platform` is the platform’s own store (people, spaces, seats), answered only to a seat in `yak`.

  yak admin query jeff/recipes .doc
  yak admin query jeff .kind=note
  yak admin query yak/platform '.person&.email.address=jeff@yak.sh' --admin

admin_client.title: Keep an OAuth client
admin_client.description:
Keep an OAuth client yaks.app signs in to a service as, sealed in the platform's vault under its name; every integration naming that client signs in as it. The id and the secret are op:// references, read here and never printed.

  yak admin client google 'op://Yak Shaving LLC/googleapis oauth/client id' 'op://Yak Shaving LLC/googleapis oauth/client secret' --admin

name.description: the client's name, as an integration's `client` names it

id.description: an op:// reference to the client id

secret.description: an op:// reference to the client secret, for a confidential client

admin_tool.title: Call a yaks.app tool as this account
admin_tool.description:
Call one yaks.app connector tool as the signed-in account rather than as the bearer `yak login` keeps, which is what a probe needs. Its own arguments follow as key=value.

  yak admin tool app_list
  yak admin tool app_new slug=notes title='Notes'

admin_push.title: Push a directory to a yaks.app app
admin_push.description:
Make an app hold exactly the files in a directory, through the connector's own tools: app_new when the app does not exist yet, app_files for every file (base64 for any that is not UTF-8), a delete for each file the directory no longer has, then app_deploy. Git is the app's only source. The app's slug is the directory's name unless --app names another; --space picks one when the account has several.

  yak admin push apps/mail --owner
  yak admin push apps/mail --app inbox --space jeff --title Inbox --owner

dir.description: the directory holding the app's files

app.description: the app's slug, when it is not the directory's name

space.description: the space, when the account has several

title.description: the title a new app is created with; the slug unless named

admin_deploys.title: List yaks.app versions and deployments
admin_deploys.description: Recent yaks.app uploads and deployments with their commits and live times; ~ marks a commit inferred by time. Migration boundaries survive code rollbacks, and unknown history refuses a rollback. --admin or --owner is required.

admin_errors.title: List yaks.app errors by Sentry issue
admin_errors.description: Every yaks.app failure from the preceding window, thrown or caught, one line per Sentry issue and the request it broke at: count, first and last seen, issue and message. Reads Sentry with the `sentry` token this box's vault keeps, and refuses without it; `admin tail` watches live traffic. --admin or --owner is required.

admin_tail.title: Follow yaks.app live events
admin_tail.description: One line per live yaks.app event: outcome, entrypoint, request and errors. Does not return until interrupted. --admin or --owner is required.

admin_rollback.title: Roll yaks.app back to a prior version
admin_rollback.description: Emergency rollback, only for a broken build path: code corrections use `yak admin revert`, since main deploys on every push. Defaults to the prior deployed version, refuses data boundaries and uncertain commits, then probes the public doors. --admin or --owner is required.

admin_revert.title: Revert a main commit and wait for it to deploy
admin_revert.description: Revert a main commit in a fresh worktree, run deno task check, land and push main, and wait up to 20m for Workers Builds to serve the revert. A failed worktree is kept. --admin or --owner is required.
